To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spinodal decomposition is responsible for multifragmenting the finite nuclear system selected at Fermi energies, and that the spinodal fragmentation is a consequence of a first-order phase transition in the nuclear matter phase diagram.

1) the multifragmentation process in central 129Xe+natSn collisions at Fermi energies is dominated by the spinodal decomposition mechanism, 2) the spinodal decomposition is the main mechanism of multifragmentation at the Fermi energy, 3) the spinodal instability is the origin of multifragementation in finite nuclear systems, 4) the spinodal fragmentation is the origin of the multifragmentation in finite nuclear matter.

1) the charge correlation function of multifragmentation is sensitive to the spinodal decomposition in the Fermi-energy regime, 2) the spinodal decomposition is the dominant mechanism for the multifragmentation in this regime.

the investigation of the nuclear matter phase transitions in the multifragmenting systems produced in the reactions 129Xe + natSn at 32, 45 and 50 AMeVe and 129Xe+natSn at 32 and 39 AMeV.
the study of the multifragmentation process of hot nuclear matter produced in central 129Xe + natSn collisions at incident energies of 32, 45 and 50 AMe V.
the study of the dynamics of the nuclear liquid-gas phase transition.
